hero.title: Interfaces for the world.
hero.lead: An interface is the layer a person meets a system through: a visitor and a place, a citizen and an institution, a musician and a sound. We build the missing human side, for ourselves and for the businesses that hire us.

content.title: Responsibility for content
content.body: {siteName} is responsible for the content published on {host}. We write it ourselves and keep it current to the best of our knowledge. Descriptions of our own software state what is live, what is a demonstration, and what is not built yet.

links.title: External links
links.body: This site links to pages operated by other people — repositories, client sites, third-party services. Their operators are responsible for what those pages contain. We check a link when we add it; we cannot check it continuously. Tell us at <mail>{email}</mail> if one is broken or wrong and we will remove or correct it.

copyright.title: Copyright
copyright.body: Text, images, and code published on this site belong to {siteName} unless another owner is named. Quote us with a source link. Ask before reproducing a page in full.

form.title: The contact form
form.body: The form on our <link>contact section</link> submits the name, email address, company, topic, and message you type. We store that submission and send it to ourselves by email so we can answer you — answering you is the whole legal basis (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b): steps you asked us to take before a contract). Three services carry it: Vercel serves this site and runs the form, Resend delivers the email, and Google Workspace holds our inbox. We keep a message as long as the conversation it belongs to, then delete it. We do not use it for anything else and we do not sell it. Ask us to delete your message at hello@intrface.eu and we will.

ContactForm.messageLabel: What is hard to understand, slow to operate, or difficult to trust?
ContactForm.sentBody: It landed with us. The reply comes from {email}, within one working day.
ContactForm.fallbackFailed: We could not store the message just now.
ContactForm.fallbackMailClient: This form hands the message to your mail app.
ContactForm.fallbackTail: Your mail app should have opened with everything filled in. If it did not, send it to <mail>{email}</mail>.
ContactForm.errorEmail: We need an address we can reply to.
ContactForm.errorMessage: A sentence or two about the system is enough.
